title: Sara Duterte trial dates on Nov. 26 and 27 reset over defense witnesses' unavailability

blocks.text: Day 45 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial ended with a brief, tense moment as Senate impeachment presiding officer Francis Escudero announced the new schedule for the remainder of the year.

Escudero initially listed November 26 and 27, as well as December 1 to 4, and then December 7 to 11 as trial dates. If needed, additional dates could be added before December 18. However, lead defense counsel Sheila Sison raised a concern about the schedule.

“Our next witnesses are not available on 26 and 27, also given that we were only informed today that there will be hearings for next week, and as you know your honor, this is not our only commitment, so we have also already made some commitments in our other engagements,” Sison said.

“We are not interested in a protracted, prolonged trial of this case. And as this court has seen, the defense has been prudent with the time of this court has not abused this court, and has not wasted three months of time for presenting witnesses,” she added.
House prosecutor Terry Ridon moved to strike off the record Sison’s statement on wasting time, but the latter argued that it was a fact.
“It was not wasted, your honor. That needs to be clear,” Ridon said.
Escudero would later ask Sison to revise her statement from “waste” to “spend a lot of time.” Sison agreed.

“We cancel the 26 and the 27 given the fact that counsel for the respondent and witnesses are not available… We shall resume witness when your witness will be available on December 1. And we shall have four trial dates that week: 1, 2, 3 and 4.”
There will also be five trial days in the following week as needed, Escudero said. The trial is set from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.

“It is my hope that we can decide, one way or another, on this matter and on this case before we adjourn as a Congress and before the year is over. Again, one way or the other, so that both as a country and as a people, we can move forward accordingly, whatever the outcome of the trial may be,” Escudero said. —LDF, GMA News
